standard.title: Gassing of Insulating Liquids Under Electric Stress and Ionization — Part 2: Method of Determination of Gassing Rate Under Nitrogen Atmosphere (विद्युत तनाव और आयनीकरण के तहत विद्युतरोधी तरल पदार्थों का गैसिंग — भाग 2: नाइट्रोजन वातावरण के तहत गैसिंग दर के निर्धारण की विधि)

sectional_committee.name: Fluids for Electrotechnical Applications Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard (Part 2) prescribes the test method, apparatus setup, gas saturation conditions, and reporting procedures for determining the gassing rate (the tendency to evolve or absorb gas) of liquid dielectrics when subjected to high electrical stress and ionization at a gas-liquid interface under a nitrogen atmosphere over long durations.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Testing Standard. However, under national transformer procurement specifications (such as state electricity boards, Power Grid Corporation of India, and major utility specifications), insulating mineral oils and synthetic esters must carry test certificates verifying their gassing tendency per IS 12475 to prevent operational gas buildup, gas bubbling, and dielectric tracking.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, gassing rates (in mm³/min), or gas volumes must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The gassing cell must be subjected to a stable, sinusoidal high-voltage potential of 12 kV at power frequency (50 Hz or 60 Hz) to initiate localized ionization at the gas-liquid interface.
The entire gassing cell assembly must be immersed in a thermostatically controlled oil/liquid bath maintained at a stable temperature of 80 ± 0.5°C throughout the test duration.
The gas phase inside the cell must consist of high-purity nitrogen gas, which is bubbled through the liquid sample prior to the test to achieve complete gas saturation.

Due to the slow kinetics of gas evolution/absorption under nitrogen, the test must be maintained continuously for 18 hours (for 50 Hz systems) or 15 hours (for 60 Hz systems) to obtain a representative cumulative gassing rate.
Results are reported as the net change in gas volume (in mm³) or as a normalized gassing rate (in mm³/min) calculated from pressure changes or burette liquid level movement.
To ensure statistical validity, the gassing test must be performed on at least duplicate specimens, and their results must satisfy standard repeatability criteria.

Duplicate test runs are considered suspect and must be repeated if their calculated gassing tendencies differ by more than a specified repeatability threshold (typically 0.3 + 0.26·|G| mm³/min, where G is the mean gassing value).

To prevent cross-contamination and solvent residue staining, the borosilicate glass cell and electrodes must be thoroughly cleaned with n-heptane, petroleum ether, or 1,1,1-trichloroethane and dried completely before refilling.

Because the test involves a combination of high-voltage ionization (12 kV), heated flammable oils (80°C), and pressurized gases, a secure, transparent safety shield must be installed around the gassing cell to protect laboratory operators.
